title: Strazz Robinhood MCP
tagline: An MCP server for market research and risk-managed trading
summary: A Model Context Protocol server that gives an AI assistant structured access to market research and portfolio state — quotes, fundamentals, filings, macro series, and signals — alongside an execution path that is explicitly risk-gated and defaults to paper trading. It grew past a single server into a small system: a Python tool surface, a C# gateway and quant service, and a React chat client.
highlights: Built on MCP, so the same tool surface works with any MCP-capable client rather than being tied to one assistant.
Research and execution are separate tool groups: nothing reaches an order without passing risk checks, and paper trading is the default path rather than an option.
Pulls from primary sources — SEC EDGAR filings, FRED macro series, congressional trading disclosures, and Kalshi prediction markets — instead of a single vendor feed.
Backtesting, factor modelling, and a pick tracker make the strategies measurable rather than anecdotal.
Roughly 56 test modules alongside linting and coverage tooling, because the logic touches real money.
methodology: Exposed brokerage and research capabilities as discrete MCP tools with typed inputs, so an assistant composes them instead of scraping.
Separated read-only research tools from anything capable of placing an order, and routed every order through explicit risk and exposure checks.
Made a sandbox paper-trading path the default, so the system can be exercised end to end without risking capital.
Integrated primary data sources — EDGAR filings, FRED macro series, congressional disclosures, and Kalshi markets — behind a consistent tool interface.
Added backtesting, factor models, and prediction tracking so signal quality can be measured over time.
Split out a C# gateway and quant service plus a React chat client, keeping the MCP server itself focused on the tool surface.
Kept credentials strictly in environment configuration, never in the repository.

gallery.caption: Architecture — research tools are read-only; every order passes risk checks and runs against the paper-trading sandbox unless live trading is explicitly enabled
